newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - February 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - February 14.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Thousands of mourners flock in buses, tractors and lorries to pay last respects to slain ruling People's Alliance (PA) lawmaker Nalanda Ellawala. Ellawala was gunned down in Kuruwita near Ratnapura, in central Sri Lanka on Tuesday, a day before nominations closed for local government polls on March 21.
Opposition United National Prty (UNP) leader Ranil Wickremesinghe asks two party men wanted by police in connection with killing of Nalanda Ellawala, to give themselves up.
Police offer million-rupee reward for information leading to arrest of UNP's Susantha Punchinilame and Mahinda Ratnatilleke. The two are wanted in connection with killing of Nalanda Ellawala.
Nalanda Ellawala told medical staff in the hospital who shot him, informed sources say. Ellawala succumbed to his injuries at Ratnapura hospital in central Sri Lanka.
State functions cancelled until February 16, as mark of respect to slain lawmaker Nalanda Ellawala, whose funeral is on February 15.
Gamini Rajapakse of Ratnapura, a UNP candidate in the forthcoming local government elections, resigned on Thursday in protest over slaying of Nalanda Ellawala.
UNP candidate in forthcoming local government polls, Mahinda Rajapakse, resigns in protest at killing of Nalanda Ellawala.

UNP leader says Susantha Punchinilame contacted him on phone soon after shooting incident in Ratnapura, where Nalanda Ellawala was killed. Punchinilame is wanted by police for questioning in connection with the shooting.

UNP leader asks if mob violence is a substitute for the due process of the law, after homes and shops of partymen were burnt in Ratnapura, following death of district member of parliament, Nalanda Ellawala.

Estranged brother of President Kumaratunga, Anura Bandaranaike who is now with the UNP, will file court action against police searching his house allegedly without a search warrant, UNP sources say. Police reportedly searched his home on information that Susantha Punchinilame was hiding there.
